heroHeadline: PLA 9 Sorties May 25 (8 Enter SW/E ADIZ — Re-Escalation From May 24 Pullback); Finance Committee Hearings Commence on NT$295B Arms Budget; 6 Days to HIMARS Deadline
heroSubtitle: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 9 PLA aircraft sorties on May 25, 2026 — 8 of 9 entering the southwestern and eastern ADIZ sectors — a moderate re-escalation from the 4-sortie pullback on May 24 and consistent with PLA's established spike-then-pullback-then-rebuild oscillating pattern. Seven PLAN vessels and 1 official ship operated around Taiwan simultaneously. The full May 2026 sortie sequence now reads: 4→29→1→2→1→0→22→12→8→12→7→9→2→3→15→6→7→13→24→7→6→16→4→9. On the legislative front, Taiwan's Legislative Yuan Finance Committee commenced hearings on Monday May 25 on the NT$295 billion special procurement budget (HIMARS, M109A7, Javelin, TOW 2B, anti-armor drones), with a floor vote expected Wednesday-Thursday May 27-28 and only 6 days remaining before the May 31 HIMARS payment deadline. Defense Minister Wellington Koo has confirmed the government will invoke Article 84 of the Budget Act if the Legislature fails to act before the deadline. Diplomatically, Trump stated on May 21 that he was willing to speak directly with Taiwan President Lai Ching-te — the first such prospect since 1979 — while the paused $14 billion PAC-3 MSE/NASAMS package remains under Congressional scrutiny and the bipartisan PORCUPINE Act (passed House Foreign Affairs 45-0) presses the administration on advance notification requirements. Beijing's coordinated posture of PLA pressure, arms sale interference, and blocking of Elbridge Colby's Pentagon Beijing visit continues to signal that cross-strait coercion and diplomatic leverage are being applied simultaneously as the HIMARS deadline approaches.
